newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures erode late, end down.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures erode late, end down.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures finished lower, after eroding late as profit-taking incited technical pressure.

Traders said waves of sell-stops plagued September Standard and Poor's 500 futures late, pulling S&Ps to a one-week low. September slid as low as 906.50 in brisk late trade, before recovering to close mid-range but still lower.

Stock index futures started the session on a firm note as players eyed the key 8,000 level in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. But the Dow could not challenge the milestone, and jitters prevailed the rest of the day.
September S&Ps whipsawed late, first hitting sell-stops starting at 912.00, then bouncing more than 10 points.
"It's the two-o'clock volatility coming in again," one S&P 500 futures trader said.
He noted that at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, September Treasury bond futures closed just below key 114-00.
"But then (S&Ps) bounced real well," he said.
Traders said the market was vulnerable to technical trading given the week's slow data lineup. The agenda was slim Wednesday, with traders looking ahead to Friday's June producer price report.

A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of unchanged for the overall index and a 0.1 percent increase excluding the volatile food and energy sectors. In the previous report, both readings fell 0.3 percent.

Technically, the market was prone to consolidation given how close September is to record territory, traders said. September S&Ps and other indices set fresh all-time highs last Wednesday, Thursday and Monday. Traders said it was natural for the market to gyrate a bit to relieve overbought conditions.
The current record is 932.25, set Monday.

At the close, September S&P 500s were down 9.80 points at 918.00, Nasdaq 100s rose 4.25 to 1021.50, Russell 2000s were down 2.75 points at 400.10, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 295.0 to 19,640.0 and Midcap 400s fell 2.30 points to 296.90.
